newsitem.title: INDIA: Saudi jet to try liftoff from short India runway.
newsitem.headline: Saudi jet to try liftoff from short India runway.

text.p: A Saudi Arabian Airlines jumbo jet that landed by mistake at an Indian military airfield will try to take off on Friday from the compact runway where it made the screeching touch-down, officials said.

The Saudi Boeing 747 landed on Monday morning at the Tambaram Air Force airstrip instead of nearby Meenambakkam International Airport even though Indian defence officials fired red flares to warn the pilot against using the runway.

The pilot later told authorities he had mistaken the military airfield for the international airport even though the commercial airstrip is more than twice as long as Tambaram's 4,763-foot (1,452-metre) runway.
None of the 331 passengers or 17 crew were hurt in the landing, which one traveller called "rough and bumpy". The jumbo jet was on a flight from Dhahran in eastern Saudi Arabia to Madras.

The Saudi captain was questioned earlier this week by Indian investigators, and two air traffic controllers at Madras airport were suspended pending completion of the inquiry, civil aviation officials said.
Local newspapers said the radar at Madras airport was not working when the jumbo jet landed but other ground equipment was operating.
The freak landing was the latest in a series of potential air disasters in India.

Last month Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim said there had been 10 near-misses mainly involving commercial airliners in Indian airspace since the world's worst mid-air collision near New Delhi killed 349 people last November.

A senior official of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation in New Delhi said the original pilot would not be at the controls when the jet, stripped of as much weight as possible, tried to take off.
One of Saudi Arabian Airlines' most senior pilots and an experienced flight engineer would be among the handful of people on board the jet when it leaves the airbase, he said.
It will land soon after at Madras airport, about 11 km (7 miles) away.
"They are waiting for the wind to be most favourable," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

Witnesses said the jet, its tyres smoking, came to a screeching halt on Monday near the end of the runway, which is well short of the 8,500 feet (2,591 metres) length recommended for landings by Boeing 747s.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said officials planned to reduce the weight of the plane to 100 tonnes from 380 tonnes at landing to enable it to climb quickly enough to clear the end of the military airstrip.
It said officials had removed galley equipment, emptied drinking water tanks and drained most of the fuel.
